file_name: J et al. - 2023 - Designing Software for Genomics Medicine Service Leaders to Engage Stakeholders.txt

barriers.description: The study used a small sample of seven GM service leaders, limiting the breadth of end-user input available to the design team.
barriers.justification: A small participant sample constrained the team's ability to manage user understanding and evaluate designs across diverse institutional contexts, reducing confidence in requirements and prioritization for iteration.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, we performed our analysis with a sample size of seven GM service leaders.

barriers.description: A large portion of synthesized user feedback (39%) was not relevant to the design considerations, adding noise to the analysis.
barriers.justification: Irrelevant or off-target feedback increased analytic workload and hindered the team's ability to efficiently integrate feedback and prioritize design iterations and requirements.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, many of the synthesized comments were not relevant to the design considerations of focus in this work (39%, N=54).

barriers.description: Maintaining accurate, up-to-date information about potential stakeholder individuals (roles, credentials, expertise) is challenging due to changing career roles and other dynamics.
barriers.justification: Limited or unstable access to reliable stakeholder metadata prevents designers from specifying and implementing robust search and selection functionality, hindering the ability to manage user understanding and produce effective design solutions for stakeholder identification.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Feasibility to provide the most accurate and up-to-date information in requested areas, however, requires further investigation. Individuals, for example, may change career roles, employment, expertise, and location which can create challenges to maintaining such up-to-date information.

barriers.description: Unclear data access requirements limit integration of local evidence tools (e.g., PRECISE-Value) into the user process.
barriers.justification: Constraints on accessing institution-specific data prevented designers from incorporating local-evidence modeling into the prototype, hindering understanding of context of use and evaluation of design options that depend on local data.
barriers.reference_excerpt: More work is needed to understand data access requirements to incorporate such a tool into the user process.

barriers.description: The team was unable to study the relationship between stakeholder engagement and organizational readiness for GM services.
barriers.justification: This knowledge gap limited designers' ability to fully understand context of use and to translate stakeholder engagement insights into actionable design requirements and prioritization strategies.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, we were unable to study the relationship between stakeholder engagement and organizational readiness for a GM service or genetic test offering.
